result.question: How has Nvidia's data center business contributed to its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years?
result.answer:
Nvidia's total revenue grew dramatically across its last three fiscal years, from $60.9 billion in FY2024 to $130.5 billion in FY2025 and $215.9 billion in FY2026 [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2024-01-28] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-01-26] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25]. In each of these years, management attributed the revenue growth primarily to the data center business. In FY2024, demand for Nvidia's data center systems and products surged [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p001]. In FY2025, revenue growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with demand for the Hopper architecture driving significant growth for the full year [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]. In FY2026, revenue growth was again driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell architectures representing the majority of Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001]. The company's two operating segments are Compute & Networking and Graphics, and segment operating income grew from $37.9 billion in FY2024 to $88.0 billion in FY2025 and $139.3 billion in FY2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. The increase in U.S.-based revenue in FY2026 and FY2025 was primarily due to higher U.S.-based Compute & Networking segment demand [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Nvidia describes itself as now being a data center-scale AI infrastructure company reshaping all industries [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001].

### Retracted claims

The following claims could not be verified against their cited sources and were removed from the answer:
